PDF export is separate from Page publishing unless the current platform explicitly supports it.

exampleAnswers.Purpose and audience: Document scenario inputs, units, rationale, and the effect of changing assumptions.
exampleAnswers.Working context: This fictional studio planning model uses a simple monthly revenue scenario. It is a demonstration of assumption management, not a forecast of Claw Me or a recommendation about business finances.
exampleAnswers.Example records:
Input: Projects completed · Base value: 2 · Unit: Per month · Reason to revisit: Capacity changes
Input: Average project fee · Base value: 2400 · Unit: EUR per project · Reason to revisit: Scope mix changes
Input: Direct project cost · Base value: 600 · Unit: EUR per project · Reason to revisit: Supplier costs change
Input: Fixed operating cost · Base value: 1800 · Unit: EUR per month · Reason to revisit: Recurring commitments change
exampleAnswers.Content decisions:
Base scenario: Two projects at €2,400 produce €4,800 in modeled revenue. Subtracting €1,200 in direct project costs and €1,800 in fixed costs leaves €1,800 before items not included in this simplified model.
One-project scenario: At one project, modeled revenue is €2,400 and the same calculation leaves €0. This illustrates sensitivity to project volume; it is not a complete profit or cash-flow calculation.
What remains outside: Tax, timing, owner compensation, financing, and other relevant items are not modeled here. Add the actual inputs and have the model reviewed before relying on it for a material decision.
exampleAnswers.Format and interaction: ledger layout; section navigation and expandable detail where useful; matching portrait document PDF.
exampleAnswers.Sharing and provenance: A hypothetical example informed by Claw Me’s small-team and Agent workflows. These are not Pete’s actual clients, finances, travel plans, research results, or commitments. Keep the real adaptation private until the owner chooses to share.
